messages:
Owen: Heads up — onboarding thread for FastForge. They're seeing a burst of 429s during SDK init in staging, flow gets stuck at preflight. Any quick mitigation suggestions?
Maria: Saw the alert. They're on node-sdk v0.9.2 and doing heavy parallel preflight (hundreds at once) from serverless warmers.
Sam: That pattern screams preflight fanout + ephemeral token churn. Do we have their telemetry for token refreshes per minute?
Dev-Ops-Bot: tenant=fastforge, 5m_avg_rps=420, 429_spike_samples=37 at 11:03PT, preflight_rate_ratio=0.82
Maria: Recommend immediate client-side changes: enable keepAlive, cap concurrent preflight, and add jitter/splay between init attempts. Also ensure they cache ephemeral tokens per process instead of per request. :thinking_face:
Owen: Quick config we can drop into their app?
Maria: Yes, suggested snippet: ```js
// node-sdk example
const client = new Redwood({
  keepAlive: true,
  preflightJitterMs: 150, // random 50-250ms
  maxParallelPreflight: 6,
  tokenCacheTTLms: 60000
});
```
Sam: Also advise exponential backoff for 429s and avoid tight retry loops. If they're using serverless, recommend an init gate to serialize warmers (one-at-a-time warmup).
Rachel: I pinged their lead eng and proposed a short experiment: reduce parallel preflight to 5 and enable jitter. If that drops 429s we can roll guidance into onboarding checklist.
fastforge-eng: Thanks — applying the client changes now and will restart warmers. Will report back in ~20m.
Owen: If they still get 429s after the client changes, offer a temporary quota bump for their staging tenant while they stabilize, but only for 30–60m. Also capture their traffic profile for an infra follow-up.
Maria: Noted for the onboarding playbook update. I'll add a section on serverless warmers and preflight splay. Follow-up in 30m to confirm. :white_check_mark:
